Hi Sara / Tom 

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can line up your network team and our infra folks: 

Summary of what we heard:
- You want private connectivity from Acme VPCs into Redwood for inference endpoints (VPC Endpoints + private egress).
- Requirements: IP allowlist on the Redwood side, DNS resolution over private link, and mTLS for mutual authentication.
- You plan to use embeddings + a reranker pipeline and will call both the text-generation/chat and embeddings endpoints.

Action items / next steps:
1) Acme: share your VPC CIDR(s) and the team contact for network engineering. (Sara / Tom)
2) Acme: upload the attached spreadsheet with expected peak qps and token estimates (helps sizing).
3) Redwood: confirm supported auth modes and provide network diagrams for the VPC endpoint flow (we'll circulate a draft by EOD tomorrow).
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your network and security team  propose Tue 10/13 10:00 AM PT.

Notes on integration concerns we discussed:
- SDK/auth: our SDK supports API keys and mTLS client certs for private deployments; hosted customers can also use short-lived tokens via our private control plane when configured.
- Routing: we can pin traffic to Dedicated pools in the same region to reduce egress hops.
- Embeddings/rerank: recommend colocated batching for embeddings to reduce latency; we can provide a sample reranker using our embeddings + lightweight candidate scoring.

Attachments: 
- acme-redwood-vpc-requirements.xlsx (please fill the traffic/throughput columns)

If that matches what you expect, please confirm the team contact and whether Tue 10/13 10:00 AM PT works for a 45-min tech deep-dive.

Jonas / Marissa / Acme 

Thanks  quick technical answers below (high level) and I'll attach the one-pager and diagram in a separate email (PDF).

1) PrivateLink: supported. For hosted Redwood customers we create a service name in the customer's region; customer creates an interface endpoint in their VPC and accepts the connection (standard PrivateLink flow). We'll need the account ID and preferred region. For Dedicated/private deployments we can also accept cross-account peering or direct connect depending on procurement.

2) DNS: we recommend conditional forwarding to Redwood's private hosted zone. For AWS PrivateLink we can publish private DNS records in a managed zone we share via delegated hosted zone or provide the CNAMEs for the endpoint. Typical setup: add an override for redwood-private.acme.internal -> private IPs returned by the endpoint. We'll provide terraform examples.

3) mTLS: we accept CA-signed client certs. Requirements: TLS 1.3, ECDSA (P-256) preferred, RSA 2048 supported. Certificate must include proper SANs and be in PEM format. Rotation: we support zero-downtime rotation via a secondary cert upload endpoint  upload new cert, stage it, then promote after verification. We'll provide a sample cert CSR and curl-based upload script.

4) Egress IPs / allowlist: For PrivateLink the customer sees stable ENI private IPs  we recommend allowlisting the interface endpoint private IPs or the service's private DNS names. For customer scenarios that need public egress IPs (e.g., on-prem calls), Redwood can provide a published set of static egress IPs per region for allowlisting. We'll provide the IP list as part of the onboarding doc.

Auth recommendation for embeddings + rerank: 
- For server-to-server calls within your VPC we recommend mTLS (CA-signed certs) for strongest security and no keys in code.
- For short-lived service tokens (if you have multiple microservices), use our private control plane to mint short-lived tokens (1h TTL) bound to a service identity. SDK supports automatic token refresh.

I'll attach: redwood-vpc-setup.pdf (one-page diagram + steps) and a sample mTLS CSR + upload steps.

Lauren Bishop
Network & Platform Lead, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
